issue.title: init and validators called multiple times for classes with a custom __init__ method
issue.body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

When a model has a custom \__init__ method, all validators run twice in certain situations

- If the model is the root model, this only happens using the model_validate* functions (or TypeAdapter.validate_python, which is what happens in FastAPI)
- If the model is an attribute in another model, this also happens for a regular init call (Model(**data)), this might have  the same root cause as #12085 but im not sure about it

Im aware the docs mention that [custom inits are discoraged](https://pydantic.dev/docs/validation/dev/concepts/models/#defining-a-custom-__init__:~:text=Defining%20a%20custom%20__init__()%20is%20not%20recommended), but that is still an option that is documented, so I belive it should work, especially since a wrap validator isn't a good enough replacment in all usecases

I managed to workaround this with this, but this feels pretty hacky, and even then I needed to add some safeguard since the wrapper was called twice for internal fields

```python
from pydantic_core import core_schema

class MyBaseClass(BaseModel):

    @classmethod
    def __get_pydantic_core_schema__(
            cls, source, handler
    ):
        # Wrap the entire validation process,
        # this is done instead of a custom __init__ since this leads to bugs and double invocation of validators
        schema = handler(source)
        try:
            # If this model was already wrapped (happens if the model is used as a field on another model)
            if schema["function"]["function"] == cls._init_wrapper:
                return schema
        except (KeyError, TypeError):
            pass

        # Otherwise, wrap it in our "custom init"
        return core_schema.no_info_wrap_validator_function(
            cls._init_wrapper,
            schema
        )

    @classmethod
    def _init_wrapper(cls, v, handler):
        # Extra init logic here
        instance = handler(v)
        return instance
```

### Example Code

```Python
from pydantic import model_validator, BaseModel

class MyBaseClass(BaseModel):
    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)

class A(MyBaseClass):

    id: int

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def a_after_validator(self):
        print("A: after_validator")
        return self


class B(MyBaseClass):

    item: A

    @model_validator(mode="wrap")
    @classmethod
    def fault_tolerate_validate(cls, value, handler):
        print('B Wrap: before handler')
        res = handler(value)
        print('B Wrap: after handler')
        return res

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def b_after_validator(self):
        print("B: after_validator")
        return self

data = {"item": {"id":1}}
B.model_validate(data)


B Wrap: before handler
B Wrap: before handler
A: after_validator
A: after_validator
B Wrap: after handler
B: after_validator
B Wrap: after handler
B: after_validator
```
